text:
maya: Heads-up: ACME just escalated — p95 and p99 spiked from ~120ms to 2.1s starting ~08:42 UTC during their rollout. They say requests are timing out occasionally.

jordan: Customer impact: webhooks and chat responses. They provided a couple of traces.

maya: I checked Console: Dedicated-pool `eu-west-3-reserved-42` shows 100% in-use and long provisioning queues. p99 correlates with 'queue wait' events.

alex: Sharing quick metrics: CPU on head nodes fine, but GPU allocation latency jumped. Looks like instance spin-up (container runtime + model load) is taking 60-120s more than usual.

sam: Could be two things: image pull/backlog or model cache population (large model). Any 500s or auth errors?

maya: No 500s. A few auth refresh retries around 08:43 but not failing. Main pattern: request enters, routes to Dedicated, then sits in "attach_wait" until GPU ready.

infra-bot: [alert] pool eu-west-3-reserved-42 saturation at 100% (since 08:40 UTC). attach_queue length: 17 -> 34. avg_provision_time increased from 18s to 95s.

alex: I queried provisioning logs. Frequent lines: `ImagePull backoff: registry throttled` and `KV-cache cold-fill: loading weights shard-3` interleaved.

maya: Repro snippet customer shared (sanitized):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"acme-chat-large","input":"hello"}' -i

Response snippet:
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
{
  "request_id": "req-abc123",
  "status": "queued",
  "detail": "waiting for compute: attach_wait"
}

jordan: They ran 50 concurrent requests which matches their rollout. That aligns with saturating the dedicated pool.

sam: Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) enable fallback routing to hosted for this customer (burst policy) 2) increase min_reserved for that pool by +2 GPUs temporarily 3) pre-pull images on spare nodes if available.

alex: Also suggest aggressive prewarm of model shards and kubernetes node imagePull concurrency tweak. But thats infra-change. Short-term: enable customer burst to hosted and reduce preferred model to a slightly smaller variant (acme-chat-medium) — customer ok with temporary downgrade?

maya: Customer accepted fallback to hosted for burst traffic. I toggled their routing to allow hosted fallback. Monitoring now.

infra-bot: [action] routing rule updated: acme -> allow_burst_hosted: true (08:55 UTC).

maya: After toggling, p95 dropped to ~220ms within two minutes for routed requests. The tail still shows attachments waiting for remaining Dedicated requests.

alex: For root cause we need to follow up on registry rate-limiting and model cache cold-fill. Two hypotheses: 1) Too many concurrent new containers pulling the same big image -> registry throttle -> spinup delay. 2) Large model shard eviction causing serial cache loads.

sam: Repro steps for eng-infra: simulate a 60-concurrency burst against a dedicated pool with min=0 and image not present on nodes; observe image pull times and attach queue. Script: 

for i in $(seq 1 60); do curl -s -X POST ... & done

Collect: attach_wait histogram, imagePullDuration, modelLoadDuration.

jordan: Customer asked for timeline and mitigations. I'll tell them: short-term fallback applied, monitoring active, next steps include increasing min_reserved and a replay for pre-pull strategy.

alex: Longer term mitigations: (a) pre-pulled immutable images for large models on dedicated clusters, (b) warm model cache during expected rollout windows, (c) implement spillover throttle that routes excess to hosted earlier (d) reduce max_concurrent_attach per pool to smooth spikes.

maya: Action items assigned: alex -> run repro and confirm registry throttle (ETA 3h). sam -> evaluate pre-pull job and min_reserved bump (ETA 1h). jordan -> notify customer with mitigation summary and ask for expected traffic windows (ongoing).

alex: Quick note: found spike of `imagePullBackoff` correlated with registry 429s at 08:41:23. I'll open infra ticket with registry team and attach logs.

sam: If registry-side fix will take time, we should script a temporary mirrored registry in same region for heavy images.

maya: Thanks all. Keeping thread open. If anyone sees p99 creep again after 09:30 UTC ping here. :thumbsup:
